doc.title: Expense payout
doc.usage: Your answers go into the development spec and are archived — if money ever goes out wrong, this receipt is what we trace it back to. Answer as things actually are; flagging what you are unsure of is worth more than a guess.

part1.we_understand: Once an expense claim is approved the system pays it out automatically; finance no longer works through a spreadsheet claim by claim.
part1.note: Tell us if this is wrong

part1.we_understand: Payments to companies need two-person review; reimbursing an employee does not — this feature is employee reimbursement, so no two-person review.

layers.why: the payable node and the partial-rejection rule decide everything else

questions.title: From which point is a claim "payable"?
questions.background: Can we pay as soon as approval passes, or does finance have to check it first? This decides when a payout is triggered.

cites.snippet: just pay it once the claim is approved

options.label: Payable as soon as approval passes
Finance has to check it first

reveal.ask: How soon must the finance check be done

demo.given: a claim approved on 2026-03-01; finance finishes its check on 2026-03-03 (the extra step under option B)

rows.v: in the 03-01 batch, employee paid the same day
in the 03-03 batch, employee paid two days later

questions.title: How does the payout batch run?
questions.background: You said "don't pay several times a day" and "run it again a few days later". We need that as a concrete rule before we can build it.

cites.snippet: don't pay several times a day
run it again a few days later

options.label: One batch a day, auto-retry up to 3 times
options.cost: the retry limit is explicit, so when money does not arrive you can tell which retry failed

options.label: One batch a week, triggered by hand
Hand it to a person to chase
Hold it and try again in the next batch

questions.title: What counts as "paid"?
questions.background: Today the code marks a claim paid as soon as the transfer is initiated. If the bank bounces it back (wrong account number, name mismatch), the claim is already marked paid while the money never reached the employee.

cites.logic: once the amount already paid reaches the approved amount, no further transfer is initiated — the claim counts as done at initiation, not at bank confirmation

branches.cond: payable and not yet paid in full
branches.then: initiate a transfer, up to 3 retries

options.label: Mark it paid as soon as the transfer is initiated (what the code does today; nothing to change)
Mark it paid only once the bank confirms (bounced claims go back to unpaid)

demo.given: a claim approved for 600, transfer initiated successfully, bounced by the bank the next day for "name mismatch"

rows.v: claim stays marked paid, nothing further is initiated
claim goes back to unpaid and joins the next batch

questions.title: A claim only partly approved — do we still pay it automatically?
questions.background: Only part of the amount was approved: do we pay the approved part, or hand it to a person?

evidence.weak: No evidence at all: nobody has ever mentioned partial rejection. We derived this question from our blind-spot checklist. If partial rejection cannot happen in your process, say the question does not hold and we will drop it.

options.label: Pause and hand it to a person

demo.given: a claim for 1000, of which only 600 was approved and 400 rejected

rows.v: 600 goes out in the normal batch
nothing goes out; it waits in a manual queue

na.note: question 2 chose B — one batch a week triggered by hand, so there are no automatic retries to begin with

clash.why: Question 2 option A means a daily job sweeps up claims and pays them out; question 3 option B means partly-approved claims wait for a person. Will the sweep pick up the claims sitting in that manual queue and pay them anyway? Who keeps them out?
